posts.topic: Computer conversations in one Chats list
posts.release_status: Development update; not an npm release announcement
posts.body:
A recent Pocket Dev improvement we’ve been working on: finding the conversation you started on your computer, right from your phone.

In the development version, Chats brings recent computer conversations into the same screen as your Pocket Dev chats. Search by title, project or provider, then open the conversation you want to continue.

The first page also refreshes quietly while the list is open, so starting a new conversation on your computer doesn’t always mean reaching for Refresh on your phone.

The goal is simple: fewer steps between “I need to check that” and seeing your work.

This is a development update, not a release announcement. Your computer still needs to stay on and awake; access away from the same Wi-Fi needs optional remote setup.

Project: https://www.theani.me/work/pocket-dev
Source: https://github.com/anisirji/pocket-dev

posts.topic: Following a busy conversation before handing it over
posts.release_status: Development work; real cross-platform handover validation remains incomplete
posts.body:
What should happen when you open a coding conversation on your phone while the computer is still answering?

That’s one of the handover details we’ve been improving in Pocket Dev.

The development flow lets the phone follow the reply and current step while the computer’s program still owns the conversation. New messages wait in a queue. Once the program is idle, Pocket Dev can hand the conversation over so you can continue from the phone.

We’re also working through Windows-specific process handling and the cases where another program still holds the conversation.

This remains development work. Real-world handover checks across the supported apps and platforms are still needed.

The aim: keep the context when you step away from your desk, without interrupting work just to look at it.

Project: https://www.theani.me/work/pocket-dev
Source: https://github.com/anisirji/pocket-dev

posts.topic: Separate camera, gallery and document choices
posts.release_status: Development update; real-phone validation remains incomplete
posts.body:
A small mobile detail we’re improving in Pocket Dev: choosing how to attach something.

“Take a photo,” “pick something from my gallery,” and “choose a document” are three different intentions. A single file picker doesn’t always make those choices clear.

We’ve separated them in the development version:

• Take photo — ask for the camera directly.
• Photos and videos — use the media picker.
• Files — choose documents.

These choices apply to the chat and terminal attachment controls and the Files screen. The desktop browser keeps its normal picker.

This is a development update. Real-phone checks are still needed, especially for how different Android browsers open their pickers.

Small interactions like this matter when your phone is the only screen in your hand.

posts.topic: Shorter setup pages and a gentle sharing invitation
posts.release_status: Published website features; checked live on 18 November 2026
posts.body:
We shortened Pocket Dev’s setup pages and added an easier way to pass it along.

The essentials are visible first. Longer reference material and full prompts expand when you need them. The setup guide also includes the existing macOS installation video.

There’s a copyable setup prompt for your AI assistant, plus a Share button on the product, setup and prompts pages. On browsers that support sharing it opens the share sheet; otherwise it copies the message for you.

We want the first steps to feel easier, whether you follow the guide yourself or ask your AI to help.

And there’s a gentle invitation at the end: if Pocket Dev makes your day a little freer, share it with three people you’d love to see escape the PC cage too. No pressure. ❤️
